dedupe_keys.name: usgs did you feel it dyfi crowdsourced earthquake felt reports and community intensity maps with archive search and yearly data viewer

description: Did You Feel It? is the US Geological Survey's citizen science system that collects reports from people who felt an earthquake and turns them into maps of shaking intensity and damage. The pages read on 2026-09-28 describe felt event lists for the past day, week and month, a search of past earthquakes that have DYFI products, a yearly viewer of cumulative response maps for the United States and the world, and a scientific background page explaining the questionnaire, how answers are aggregated into community intensities, the relation to the Modified Mercalli scale and ShakeMap, and the intensity algorithm. The background notes uses such as feeding ShakeMap, checking national seismic hazard maps, and comparing intensity with building safety tags after the Napa 2014 earthquake. Coverage is global, with dense responses in the United States. Access is free; no licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: reports depend on who responds, so sparsely populated areas are thin, and intensities are aggregated by postal code or grid cell, not per building. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response studies, such as validating ground-shaking scenarios against observed intensities at infrastructure sites. Related records: USGS PAGER alerts and its global building inventory.
